Releasing MixOS

The first release target is Linux x86_64 with a glibc 2.39 floor. The release contract is in tools/release_packages.mx. The initial desktop candidate contains one archive, release.manifest.mx, and SHA256SUMS.txt. The desktop archive includes the ten desktop products, indexd and the Mix runtime used by its session scripts. An admitted server archive can join a later candidate. Every archive in a candidate comes from one exact public source commit. Packaging an unadmitted service does not admit it for publication.

Build and gate

Use a designated CBC worker and freeze a full 40-character source commit. tools/release_gate.mix check --commit SHA runs format, workspace build, Clippy, functional tests, the release-mode editd latency test, source gates and Mix tests. Its LOG lines identify the saved stage logs. The operator records mixos/weekly-x86_64-full as green only when this complete gate passes at that same commit. There is no Rust build on a GitHub push.

For packaging, prepare a signed Ubuntu 24.04 root with glibc 2.39, the pinned Rust toolchain from rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo's cache, and the development libraries used by the workspace: libxkbcommon-dev, libwayland-dev, libx11-dev, libxrandr-dev, libxi-dev, libxcursor-dev, libgl1-mesa-dev, libegl-dev, libgles-dev, libgbm-dev, libdrm-dev, libinput-dev, libudev-dev, libseat-dev, libpixman-1-dev, libpulse-dev, libpipewire-0.3-dev and libspa-0.2-dev. It also needs git, build-essential, pkg-config, clang, libarchive-tools, meson, ninja-build and patchelf. Ubuntu 24.04 supplies libinput 1.25, while compd's tablet dial support uses the 1.26 ABI. Build libinput 1.26.2 from upstream tag 1.26.2 (peeled commit 3402f380019dc4f882e1d8627029607aca3f4be6) inside the same root with Meson, install it under /usr, and run ldconfig there. Keep that pinned source checkout inside the target directory. The gate refuses another libinput source or library version. The desktop archive bundles the 1.26.2 shared library and its licence; compd's relative runtime library path makes that copy take precedence over the host copy. After installing the listed build dependencies in the root, the CBC worker can provision the pinned library with:

/opt/mixos/bin/mix tools/libinput_compat.mix \
  --rootfs /srv/ubuntu-24.04-root --target-dir /srv/mixos-target

The script verifies the upstream commit and installed ABI. It is safe to run again after an Ubuntu root update. On the CBC worker, the native Mix gate takes absolute paths for the root, Cargo and Rustup homes, and a dedicated target directory. It bind-mounts the exact checkout, toolchain, cache, target, /proc and /dev/null into the root, checking each mount's identity. It refuses a root that does not report glibc 2.39 or does not see the requested commit.

mix tools/release_gate.mix package --commit FULL_SHA --version V \
  --package desktop \
  --rootfs /srv/ubuntu-24.04-root --target-dir /srv/mixos-target \
  --cargo-home /home/user/.cargo --rustup-home /home/user/.rustup \
  --libinput-source /srv/mixos-target/libinput-1.26.2-src \
  --out /srv/mixos-target/release-V

The package stage builds each selected Cargo package once in that root. The packager then runs each binary's --version inside the same root, checks the source hash and bundled libinput resolution, and writes the archives and manifest. The --fixture-binaries option is for tests only; the gold installer refuses fixture manifests. Check the complete saved log and the archive hashes before upload. Never substitute a build made against a newer host glibc.

Stage and publish

Transfer the three desktop output files from CBC with a hash comparison on both sides. Upload them to a new draft GitHub Release at the frozen commit, then compare GitHub's asset digests with the CBC files. Do not replace an existing published tag or its assets. Publishing requires a full green status, archive checks, clean install and rollback proof, and acceptance for every included archive. The release notes identify any archive that is still pending. Enable immutable releases before public publication.

After the initial release, cut one candidate each week. Failure holds the previous release; it does not trigger repeated rebuilds on every push.

Install the system gold tree

The operator supplies the manifest hash from the verified GitHub asset digest. plan makes no gold changes. apply needs one explicit privileged invocation, and prints a receipt ID for rollback. The installer refuses a missing or changed archive, wrong source or architecture, a glibc floor above the host, and unsafe archive paths.

sudo /opt/mixos/bin/mix tools/gold_release.mix plan \
  --manifest /path/to/release.manifest.mx --manifest-sha256 TRUSTED_SHA256 \
  --archive-dir /path/to/assets --package desktop

sudo /opt/mixos/bin/mix tools/gold_release.mix apply \
  --manifest /path/to/release.manifest.mx --manifest-sha256 TRUSTED_SHA256 \
  --archive-dir /path/to/assets --package desktop

Install and activate are separate operations. A shared desk sees the host gold tree through its mount. An isolated desk needs a hash-checked copy of that tree and its own restart. Test the isolated desk first, then the shared desk. The public installer does not assume particular console numbers. Prefs currently tracks and installs MixOS releases per user; it does not update or restart a system desk.
